chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd, who said: I came to al-Rida (AS) asking him about Divine Unity.

He dictated to me: All praise be to Allah, the Originator of things by creation and the Initiator of them by inception, through His Power and Wisdom. Not from anything, lest creation be invalidated, nor for a cause, lest inception be invalid. He created what He willed, how He willed, being One in that, without manifestation of His Wisdom or reality of His Lordship. Intellects cannot grasp Him, imagination cannot reach Him, eyes cannot perceive Him, and scale cannot encompass Him. Speech is incapable without Him, eyes are expressionless without Him, and descriptions go astray in Him. He is hidden without a veiled veil, and covered without a covered covering. He is known without seeing, described without an image, and characterized without a body. There is no god but Allah, the Great, the Most Exalted.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological understanding of Divine Unity and Allah's attributes of transcendence?
ai.summary: This dictation by Imam al-Rida (AS) serves as a cornerstone of Shia theological discourse on *Tawhid*, explicitly rejecting anthropomorphism (*Tashbih*) and corporealism (*Jism*) by affirming that Divine attributes are real yet distinct from physical bodies. It highlights the epistemological limit of human perception, asserting that while Allah is known and described, He remains transcendent beyond the grasp of intellects, senses, and linguistic expression. This passage is frequently cited in *Usul al-Kafi* and *al-Tawhid* to establish the doctrine of Divine Simplicity and the negation of spatial or temporal containment.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma`il ibn Bazi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd that I came to (`Ali) al-Rida (AS) asking him about Divine Unity, so he (AS) dictated to me:

All praise be to Allah, the Originator, Producer, and Innovator [Mubtadi`] of all things from the beginning by His Power and Wisdom, not from anything that could invalidate His Invention, nor for nay wrong cause. He created whatever He wanted how He wanted, and He did so independently in order to manifest His Wisdom, and the Reality of His Lordship. Intellects cannot grasp Him. Imagination cannot reach Him. Eyes cannot perceive Him, and scale cannot encompass Him. Speech is incapable without Him. Eyes are expressionless without Him, and rhetoric of description goes astray in Him. He is hidden without a veil and is covered without a covering. He is recognized without seeing. He is described without an image. And He is praised despite the face that He does not possess a body. There is no god but Allah, the great, the Most Exalted.”
